name: application-copy-share-link-row
title: Copy Share Link Row
description: Read-only share link with a Copy button that writes to the clipboard and confirms with "Copied!", plus a link-permission select.
useWhen: Sharing a generated link (invite, document, recording) where the recipient needs to copy it in one click.
The link's access level is user-configurable (view/edit/invite-only) and should live right next to the link itself.
You want built-in visual confirmation that the copy action succeeded, not just a silent clipboard write.
avoidWhen: You're copying an arbitrary value with no permission concept (API key, ID) — use the simpler `copy-field` instead.
Sharing needs a full flow (invite by email, member list, role assignment) — use `share-dialog`, which this row is a building block for.
The link's permission is fixed and not user-configurable — drop the select and keep just the input + Copy button.
responsiveBehavior: Input and Copy button share a flex row with the input shrinking; the permission select and expiry label sit in a second row below.
accessibility: The read-only input has an associated <label> naming it explicitly as the share link, not just a placeholder.
The Copy button's label changes to "Copied!" as real, user-visible text feedback — not a toast that could be missed or a color-only change.
The permission select has an associated (visually hidden) label describing it as the link's permission control.
Clipboard write failures are caught silently, leaving the read-only field manually selectable as a fallback — the UI doesn't claim success it didn't achieve.

variants.title: Copy Share Link Row
variants.description: Read-only link, Copy button, a view/edit/invite-only permission select, and an expiry label.
accessibility: Copy uses the real navigator.clipboard API and reverts its confirmation label after a timeout, not a permanent state change.

variants.title: Copy Share Link Row (Dark)
variants.description: Copy share link row adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Text and border colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
